questions.q: What is the function of the plasma membrane?
questions.solution: One of the most important functions of the plasma membrane is the transport of the molecules across it. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it. Many molecules can move briefly across the membrane without any requirement of energy and this is called the passive transport. Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by the process of simple diffusion along the concentration gradient, i.e., from higher concentration to the lower. Water may also move across this membrane from higher to lower concentration. Movement of water by diffusion is called osmosis. As the polar molecules cannot pass through the nonpolar lipid bilayer, they require a carrier protein of the membrane to facilitate their transport across the membrane. A few ions or molecules are transported across the membrane against their concentration gradient, i.e., from lower to the higher concentration. Such a transport is an energy dependent process, in which ATP is utilised and is called active transport, e.g., Na+/K+ Pump.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: A few ions or molecules are transported across the membrane against their concentration gradient, i.e., from lower to the higher concentration. Such a transport is an energy dependent process, in which ATP is utilised and is called active transport, e.g., Na+/K+ Pump.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Algae have cell walls made of minerals
Reason: Algal cell walls constitutes of pectins and proteins
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: . Algae have cell wall, made of cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals like calcium carbonate.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Primary cell wall is essential for young plants
Reason: Primary cell wall forms as the cells mature
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: The cell wall of a young plant cell, the primary wall is capable of growth, which gradually diminishes as the cell matures
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Calcium pectate is present in middle lamella
Reason: Calcium pectate is important for the growth of cell wall
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate which holds or glues the different neighbouring cells together.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Chloroplast, mitochondria and peroxisomes are considered as part of endomembrane system
Reason: All the these cell organelles are in coordination with endoplasmic reticulum
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Since the functions of the mitochondria, chloroplast and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the above components, these are not considered as part of the endomembrane system.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Endoplasmic reticulum divides the intercellular space into three distinct compartments
Reason: The three compartments are luminal, extra luminal and peripheral
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: ER divides the intracellular space into two distinct compartments, i.e., luminal (inside ER) and extra luminal (cytoplasm) compartments.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Rough endoplasmic is involved in synthesis of lipid
Reason: Ribosomes faciliate production of lipid like steroidal hormones
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: RER is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. They are extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is involved in protein synthesis
Reason: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum helps to produce protein and in its secretion
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for synthesis of lipid. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Golgi bodies contain only a fixed number of cisternae
Reason: The cisternae are arranged near the endoplasmic reticulum
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: Varied number of cisternae are present in a Golgi complex. The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the mitochondria
Reason: Golgi cisternae have concave cis and convex trans face
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis or the forming face and concave trans or the maturing face.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Golgi apparatus remains in close association with mitochondria
Reason: Packaged materials are transported to the mitichondria through the cis face
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face. This explains, why the golgi apparatus remains in close association with the endoplasmic reticulum.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Golgi apparatus is the site for the formation of chitin and cellulose
Reason: Chitin and cellulose molecules modifies in the cisternae of golgi bodies
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: A number of proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the golgi apparatus before they are released from its trans face. Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Lysosomes are capable of synthesizing carbohydrates, proteins and lipids
Reason: They contain enzymes like kinase and synthetase that help in producing different molecules
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: Lysosomes very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Concentration in vacuoles is lower than that in cytoplasm
Reason: Tonoplast facilitates the transport of ions outside the vacuoles
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: In plants, the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole, hence their concentration is significantly higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The number of mitochondrions vary in different cells
Reason: It depends on the the physiological activity of the cells
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: The number of mitochondria per cell is variable depending on the physiological activity of the cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Each mitochondrion is a triple membrane bound structure
Reason: The three membranes divide the mitochondrion into aqueous compartments
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: Each mitochondrion is a double membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane and the inner membrane dividing its lumen distinctly into two aqueous compartments.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Mitochondria are the sites of anerobic respiration
Reason: They produce energy in the form of lactic acid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Leucoplasts can store nutrients
Reason: Majority of the chromoplasts of the green plants are found in the palisade cells of the leaves.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Thylakoids help in photosynthesis
Reason: A number of organised flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids, are present in the stroma
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
questions.solution: Chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids and contribute to photosynthesis
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Leucoplasts are colorless plastids
2. Amyloplasts store proteins
3. Chloroplasts contain cartenoid
4. The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is called the stroma.
5. A number of organised flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids, are present in the stroma
questions.solution: The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. 70s ribosome has 60s and 40s subunits
2. 80s ribosome have 50s and 30s subunits
3. Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade. They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins.
4. They are not surrounded by any membrane.
questions.solution: The two subunits of 80S ribosomes are 60S and 40S while that of 70S ribosomes are 50S and 30S.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Chloroplasts can be found in mesophyll cells
2. Chloroplasts are single membrane bound
3. Stroma are flatenned membranous sac 4.The ribosomes of the chloroplasts are 80 s.
questions.solution: Majority of the chloroplasts of the green plants are found in the mesophyll cells of the leaves. These are lens-shaped, oval, spherical, discoid or even ribbon-like organelles having variable length (5-10µm) and width (2-4µm).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Movement of water by diffusion is called passive transport
2. Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model.
3.One of the most important functions of the plasma membrane is the transport of the molecules across it.
4. Movement of water by diffusion is called osmosis.
5. In human beings, the membrane of the erythrocyte has approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids.
questions.solution: An improved model of the structure of cell membrane was proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972) widely accepted as fluid mosaic model.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Stroma contains enzymes
2. Grana is the membrane covering thylakoids
3. Thylakoids are arranged into piles called lumen.
4. The membrane of the thylakoids enclose a space called a lumen.
5. The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins.
questions.solution: The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Passive transport requires energy
2. Active transport involves movement of ions along the concentration gradient
3.The cell wall of a young plant cell, the primary wall is capable of growth.
4. Algae have cell wall, made of cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals like calcium carbonate.
5. The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate which holds or glues the different neighbouring cells together.
questions.solution: Many molecules can move briefly across the membrane without any requirement of energy and this is called the passive transport.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. George Palade first observed mitochondria under the electron microscope
2. Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S
3. Svedbergs unit stands for dissociation coefficient
4. Cilia are large structures which work like oars.
questions.solution: The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S.The two subunits of 80S ribosomes are 60S and 40S.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Mesosome is formed from cell membrane extensions
2. Flagella is present in non motile bacterias
3. The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules.
4. The peripheral doublets are also interconnected by linkers.
5. Both the cilium and flagellum emerge from centriole-like structure called the basal bodies.
questions.solution: A special membranous structure is the mesosome which is formed by the extensions of plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Cytoskeleton consists of only microtubules
2. Cytoskeleton provides mechanical support to the cell
3. Cillia are hair like outgrowths of the mitochondria
4. The mitochondria divide by fission.
5. The inner membrane of mitochondria forms a number of infoldings called the cristae
questions.solution: The cytoskeleton in a cell are involved in many functions such as mechanical support, motility, maintenance of the shape of the cell.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Anton Von Leewenhoek first described a live cell
2. Robert Brown dicovered nucleus
3. 1838, Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, examined a large number of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells.
4. Rudolf Virchow first explained that cells divided and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.
5. Schleiden and Schwann together formulated the cell theory.
questions.solution: Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus. The invention of the microscope and its improvement leading to the electron microscope revealed all the structural details of the cell.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Flagellum lack a cell membrane
2. Axoneme is the core of a cilium
3. Axoneme has eight doublets of microtubules
4. The matrix of euakaryotic mitochondria also possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (80S)
questions.solution: The electron microscopic study of a cilium or the flagellum show that they are covered with plasma membrane. Their core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Prokaryotic flagella is structurally similar to eukaryotic flagella
2. Axonemal microtubules are arranged in 9+2 arrangement
3. The outer compartment of mitochondria is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix.
4. The largest isolated single cell is the egg of an ostrich.
5. Among multicellular organisms, human red blood cells are about 7.0 µm in diameter
questions.solution: Arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Prokaryotic cells lack membrane bound organelles
2. Eukaryotic cells contain membrane bound organelles
3. Mitochondria produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell.
4. Ribosomes are only found in eukaryotic cells.
5. In both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, a semi-fluid matrix called cytoplasm occupies the volume of the cell.
questions.solution: Besides the nucleus, the eukaryotic cells have other membrane bound distinct structures called organelles like the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the golgi complex, lysosomes, mitochondria, microbodies and vacuoles. The prokaryotic cells lack such membrane bound organelles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Centrosome contains one centriole
2. Centrsome is surrounded by pericentriolar material
3. The centrioles in centrosome lie perpendicular to each other.
4. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.
5. RER is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion
questions.solution: Centrosome is surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar materials. Both the centrioles in a centrosome lie perpendicular to each other in which each has an organisation like the cartwheel.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. The number of mitochondria per cell is constant
2. The adjacent triplets of peripheral fibrils are not linked
3. The central part of the centriole is proteinaceous
4. The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes
5. The enzymes of lysosyme work at only acidic pH
questions.solution: The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is also proteinaceous and is called the hub,
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Plastids lack pigment
2. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is crucial for protein synthesis
3. Lysosomes contain tubules cisternae
4. The hub is connected to the tubules by radial spokes
questions.solution: The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is also proteinaceous and called the hub, which is connected with tubules of the peripheral triplets by radial spokes made of protein.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Slime layer is a type of glycocalyx
2. Gram positive bactria cannot take up gram stain
3. Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
4. The golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials.
5. The cis and the trans faces of Golgi are entirely different, but interconnected.
questions.solution: Glycocalyx differs in composition and thickness among different bacteria. It could be a loose sheath called the slime layer in some,
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Flemming named the nuclear material chromosome
2. Interphase occurs when the nucleus divides
3. Perinuclear space forms a barrier between cytoplasm and nuclear materials
4. The nuclear matrix or the nucleoplasm contains nucleolus and chromatin.
5. The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm.
questions.solution: Electron microscopy has revealed that the nuclear envelope, which consists of two parallel membranes with a space between (10 to 50 nm) called the perinuclear space, forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Perinuclear membrane is present on the nucleus
2. The outer membrane of the nucleus is continuous with mitochondria
3. Nuclear envelope is interrupted by minute pores at some places
4. The nuclear pores allow only ions to pass
questions.solution: Perinuclear space forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.t. At a number of places the nuclear envelope is interrupted by minute pores, which are formed by the fusion of its two membranes.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Nucleolus and chromatin are in the nucleoplasm
2. Every cell has only one nucleus strictly
3. Contents of the nucleolus is continuous with the rest of nucleoplasm
4. Centrosome is the site of active RNA synthesis
questions.solution: The nuclear matrix or the nucleoplasm contains nucleolus and chromatin. The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of thenucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Anaphase nucleus has a loose network of fibres called chromatin
2. Chromatin contains histones
3. Chromosomes lack centromere
4. During cell division, nucleus ia observed in place of nucleus
questions.solution: Chromatin contains DNA and some basic proteins called histones, some non-histone proteins and also RNA.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria
2. Eukaryotic cells are represented by algae
3. Bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts – filament, hook and basal body.
4. The filament is the longest portion and extends from the cell surface to the outside.
questions.solution: The prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma and PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Centromere holds a single chromatid
2. Kinetochores are present on the sides of centromere
3. Chromosomes are classified into three types
4. Acrocentric chromosome has centromere located in the middle
questions.solution: Every chromosome (visible only in dividing cells) essentially has a primary constriction or the centromere on the sides of which disc shaped structures called kinetochores are present.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Inclusion bodies are membrane bound
2. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
3. In Amoeba the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion.
4. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles.
5. In plant cells the vacuoles can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell.
questions.solution: Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosomes or polysome. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Metacentric chromosome has centromere sightly away from the middle of the chromosome
2. Sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere located in the middle forming two equal chromosome arms
3. Acrocentric chromosome contains centrosome close to its end
4. Telocentric chromosome lacks a centromere
questions.solution: In case of acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Mitochondria are the sites of anaerobic respiration
2. Sub metacentric chromosome has centromere located near the end of the chromosome
3. In the chromoplasts fat soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls and others are present.
4. Elaioplasts store oils and starch
questions.solution: Telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Pilli are shortened disc like structures
2. Fimbriae are small bristle like fibres sprouting out of the cell
3. An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules and microfilaments only
4. The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is also proteinaceous and called the hub. 5.Centrosome is an organelle usually containing two cylindrical structures called centrioles.
questions.solution: The fimbriae are small bristle like fibres sprouting out of the cell. In some bacteria, they are known to help attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Lysosomes are double membrane structures
2. Plasma membrane is freely permeable
3. Microbodies are void of enzymes
4. Satellites are small fragments of chromosomes that cannot be stained
questions.solution: Sometimes a few chromosomes have non-staining secondary constrictions at a constant location. This gives the appearance of a small fragment called the satellite.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the given statements:

Statement I: Mitochondrial inner membrane encloses the matrix.

Statement II: The inner membrane forms infoldings called cristae.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but II is correct
questions.solution: The mitochondrion is bound by a double membrane. The inner membrane encloses the matrix, so Statement I is correct. The inner membrane is also thrown into a number of infoldings called cristae towards the matrix, which increase the surface area for the enzymes of oxidative phosphorylation, so Statement II is also correct. Hence both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Key ConceptsExplanation
A. Unicellular organisms1. First described a live cell
B. Cell2. Fundamental structural and functional unit of life
C. Anton Von Leeuwenhoek3. Capable of independent existence
D. Robert Brown4. Discovered the nucleus
questions.solution: Unicellular organisms are capable of independent existence, the cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of life, Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first described a live cell, and Robert Brown discovered the nucleus.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
DiscoveriesScientist
A. Nucleus1. Robert Brown
B. Live Cell2. Anton Von Leeuwenhoek
C. Cell Wall in Plants3. Theodore Schwann
D. Plasma Membrane4. Matthias Schleiden
questions.solution: Robert Brown discovered the nucleus, Anton Von Leeuwenhoek described the first live cell, Matthias Schleiden observed cell walls in plants, and Theodore Schwann identified the plasma membrane.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Components of Cell TheoryStatement
A. All living organisms1. Are composed of cells and products of cells
B. New cells2. Arise from pre-existing cells
C. Cell as the fundamental unit3. Make up tissues and organs
D. Products of cells4. Are essential for independent living
questions.solution: All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells, new cells arise from pre-existing cells, the cell is the fundamental unit necessary for independent living, and products of cells make up tissues and organs.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Contributions to Cell TheoryScientist
A. Cell theory formulation1. Rudolf Virchow
B. Explanation of cell division2. Matthias Schleiden
C. Study of plant cells3. Theodore Schwann
D. Study of animal cells4. Schleiden and Schwann
questions.solution: Schleiden and Schwann formulated the cell theory, Rudolf Virchow explained cell division, Matthias Schleiden studied plant cells, and Theodore Schwann studied animal cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Timeline of DiscoveriesYear/Period
A. First live cell observed1. 1855
B. Nucleus discovered2. 1838
C. Cell theory formulated3. 1839
D. Explanation of cell division4. 17th century
questions.solution: The first live cell was observed in the 17th century, the nucleus was discovered later, the cell theory was formulated around 1838-1839, and the explanation of cell division was provided in 1855.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cell Theory ComponentsDescription
A. All living organisms1. Are composed of cells
B. Cell division2. New cells arise
C. Products of cells3. Include tissues and organs
D. Arise from pre-existing cells4. Explained by Virchow
questions.solution: All living organisms are composed of cells, cell division was explained by Virchow, products of cells include tissues and organs, and new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cellular ComponentFunction
A. Ribosome1. Protein synthesis
B. Nucleus2. Specialized infoldings of the cell membrane
C. Plasmid3. Confers resistance to antibiotics
D. Mesosome4. Contains genetic material
questions.solution: Ribosomes are responsible for protein synthesis, the nucleus contains genetic material, plasmids confer antibiotic resistance, and mesosomes are specialized infoldings of the cell membrane
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
OrganismDescription
A. Mycoplasma1. Smallest isolated single cell
B. Bacteria2. Lacks cell wall
C. Ostrich3. 3 to 5 μm in size
D. Human red blood cell4. 7.0 μm in diameter
questions.solution: Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall, bacteria are generally 3 to 5 μm in size, the ostrich egg is the largest isolated single cell, and human red blood cells are about 7.0 μm in diameter.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cellular FunctionLocation
A. Genetic material1. Centrosome
B. Protein synthesis2. Ribosomes
C. Cellular activities3. Cytoplasm
D. Cell division4. Nucleus
questions.solution: Genetic material is located in the nucleus, protein synthesis occurs in ribosomes, cellular activities take place in the cytoplasm, and cell division is aided by the centrosome.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cell FeatureDescription
A. Naked genetic material1. Prokaryotic cells
B. Circular DNA outside the genomic DNA2. Plasmids
C. Absence of nuclear membrane3. Ribosomes
D. Non-membrane bound organelles4. Mycoplasma
questions.solution: Naked genetic material and the absence of a nuclear membrane are characteristics of prokaryotic cells. Circular DNA outside the genomic DNA is known as plasmids, and ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cell Size and ShapeExample or Feature
A. Mycoplasma1. Largest isolated single cell
B. Bacteria2. Rod-like or spherical
C. Nerve cells3. Longest cells
D. Ostrich egg4. Smallest cell (0.3 μm)
questions.solution: Mycoplasma is the smallest cell, bacteria can be rod-like or spherical, nerve cells are the longest, and the ostrich egg is the largest isolated single cell.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Unique Prokaryotic FeatureDescription
A. Cell wall1. Infoldings of cell membrane
B. Plasmid2. Small circular DNA
C. Mesosome3. Present in all prokaryotes except Mycoplasma
D. Absence of organelles4. No membrane-bound organelles
questions.solution: The cell wall is present in all prokaryotes except Mycoplasma, plasmids are small circular DNA, mesosomes are infoldings of the cell membrane, and prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
StructuresFunctions
A. Glycocalyx1. Helps in respiration and secretion processes
B. Mesosome2. Determines shape and provides structural support
C. Flagella3. Provides motility
D. Pili4. Aids in attachment to surfaces
questions.solution: Glycocalyx helps in attachment to surfaces.Mesosome is involved in respiration and secretion processes.Flagella provides motility. Pili aid in attachment to surfaces.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Bacteria TypesCharacteristics
A. Gram Positive1. Takes up Gram stain
B. Gram Negative2. Does not take up Gram stain
C. Slime Layer3. Thick and tough structure
D. Capsule4. Loose sheath
questions.solution: Gram-positive bacteria take up the Gram stain.Gram-negative bacteria do not take up the Gram stain.Slime layer is a loose sheath.Capsule is a thick and tough structure.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
ComponentsFeatures
A. Filament1. Longest portion of flagellum
B. Hook2. Elongated tubular structures
C. Pili3. Connects filament to basal body
D. Fimbriae4. Small bristle-like fibers
questions.solution: Filament is the longest portion of the flagellum.Hook connects the filament to the basal body.Pili are elongated tubular structures.Fimbriae are small bristle-like fibers.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Bacterial StructuresFunctions
A. Cell Wall1. Provides structural support
B. Plasma Membrane2. Site of protein synthesis
C. Ribosomes3. Selectively permeable and interacts with the environment
D. Plasmid4. Confers unique phenotypic characteristics
questions.solution: The cell wall provides structural support.Plasma membrane is selectively permeable and interacts with the environment.Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.Plasmid confers unique phenotypic characteristics.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
RibosomesCharacteristics
A. Size of ribosomes in prokaryotes1. 70S ribosome
B. Number of subunits in prokaryotic ribosomes2. Two subunits
C. Function of ribosomes3. Protein synthesis
D. Type of ribosome in prokaryotes4. 15 nm by 20 nm
questions.solution: Prokaryotic ribosomes are about 15 nm by 20 nm in size.They consist of two subunits.Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.The type of ribosome in prokaryotes is 70S.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Ribosome SubunitsSizes
A. Large subunit1. 50S
B. Small subunit2. Protein synthesis
C. Combined ribosome in prokaryotes3. 70S
D. Function of ribosomes4. 30S
questions.solution: The large subunit of prokaryotic ribosomes is 50S.The small subunit is 30S.Together, they form the 70S ribosome.Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Polysome ComponentsFunctions
A. mRNA1. Forms a chain
B. Ribosomes2. Site of translation
C. Polysome3. Translates mRNA
D. Protein synthesis4. Sequence to be translated
questions.solution: mRNA is the sequence to be translated.Ribosomes are the site of translation.Polysome forms a chain.Protein synthesis involves translating mRNA.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Inclusion BodiesCharacteristics
A. Reserve material1. Stored in cytoplasm
B. Membrane presence2. No membrane
C. Phosphate granules3. Found in some bacteria
D. Gas vacuoles4. Type of inclusion body
questions.solution: Reserve material is stored in the cytoplasm.Inclusion bodies are not bound by any membrane.Phosphate granules are a type of inclusion body.Gas vacuoles are found in some bacteria.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Eukaryotic Cell FeaturesComponents
A. Locomotory structures1. Organized genetic material
B. Nuclear envelope2. Surrounds the nucleus
C. Cytoskeleton3. Provides cell shape and structure
D. Chromosomes4. Aids in cell movement
questions.solution: Locomotory structures aid in cell movement.The nuclear envelope surrounds the nucleus.The cytoskeleton provides cell shape and structure.Chromosomes are organized genetic material.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Eukaryotic Cell ComponentsFunctions
A. Nuclear envelope1. Extensive compartmentalization
B. Organelles2. Contains genetic material
C. Cytoplasm3. Organized into chromosomes
D. Chromosomes4. Surrounds the nucleus
questions.solution: The nuclear envelope surrounds the nucleus.Organelles allow for extensive compartmentalization.Cytoplasm contains genetic material.Chromosomes are organized structures within the nucleus.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Components of Cell MembraneCharacteristics
A. Phospholipids1. Arranged in a bilayer
B. Cholesterol2. Present along with lipids
C. Proteins3. Found in human red blood cells
D. Carbohydrates4. Provide fluidity
questions.solution: Phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer.Cholesterol contributes to membrane fluidity.Proteins are found along with lipids.Carbohydrates are present in human red blood cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Phospholipid ArrangementCharacteristics
A. Polar head1. Towards the outer sides
B. Nonpolar tail2. Protected from aqueous environment
C. Hydrophobic tail3. Inside the membrane
D. Bilayer formation4. Phospholipid structure
questions.solution: The polar head of phospholipids is towards the outer sides.The nonpolar tail is inside the membrane.The hydrophobic tail is protected from the aqueous environment.Phospholipids form a bilayer.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Membrane ProteinsTypes
A. Peripheral proteins1. Partially or totally buried in the membrane
B. Integral proteins2. Lie on the surface of the membrane
C. Membrane fluidity3. Allows lateral movement
D. Bilayer4. Structural component
questions.solution: Peripheral proteins lie on the surface of the membrane.Integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the membrane.Membrane fluidity allows lateral movement.The bilayer is a structural component of the membrane.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Membrane TransportProcesses
A. Passive transport1. Requires energy
B. Active transport2. No energy required
C. Simple diffusion3. Movement along concentration gradient
D. Osmosis4. Movement of water
questions.solution: Passive transport does not require energy.Active transport requires energy.Simple diffusion involves movement along the concentration gradient.Osmosis is the movement of water.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Active TransportCharacteristics
A. ATP utilization1. Energy-dependent process
B. Carrier proteins2. Requires ATP
C. Na+/K+ Pump3. Uses specific proteins
D. Against concentration gradient4. Transports ions
questions.solution: Active transport requires ATP utilization.Carrier proteins are specific for the transport process.The Na+/K+ Pump transports ions.Active transport works against the concentration gradient
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Fluid Mosaic ModelCharacteristics
A. Proposed by Singer and Nicolson1. Describes membrane structure
B. Quasi-fluid nature2. Enables protein movement
C. Lateral movement of proteins3. Accepted in 1972
D. Model acceptance4. Describes lipid bilayer
questions.solution: The fluid mosaic model was proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972.It describes the quasi-fluid nature of the lipid bilayer.The lateral movement of proteins is enabled by the membrane's fluidity.This model describes the overall structure of the cell membrane.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Membrane Model FeaturesCharacteristics
A. Lipid bilayer1. Provides membrane stability
B. Proteins2. Allows protein movement
C. Cholesterol3. Major structural component
D. Fluidity4. Interacts with lipids and proteins
questions.solution: The lipid bilayer is the major structural component of the membrane.Proteins interact with lipids and contribute to membrane fluidity.Cholesterol provides stability to the membrane.Fluidity allows for the lateral movement of proteins within the membrane.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Components of Algal Cell WallComponents of Other Plant Cell Walls
A. Cellulose1. Cellulose
B. Galactans2. Hemicellulose
C. Mannans3. Pectins
D. Calcium carbonate4. Proteins
questions.solution: Algal cell walls contain cellulose, galactans, mannans, and calcium carbonate.Other plant cell walls contain cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Functions of Cell WallCharacteristics of Cell Wall
A. Gives shape to the cell1. Provides structural support
B. Protects from mechanical damage2. Guards against infections
C. Cell-to-cell interaction3. Restricts entry of large molecules
D. Barrier to undesirable macromolecules4. Facilitates communication
questions.solution: The cell wall gives shape, protects from damage, aids in cell interaction, and acts as a barrier to large molecules.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Faces of Golgi ApparatusCharacteristics
A. Cis face1. Maturing face
B. Trans face2. Forming face
C. Cisternae3. Flattened sacs
D. Vesicles4. Transport materials
questions.solution: The cis face is the forming face, the trans face is the maturing face, cisternae are flattened sacs, and vesicles transport materials.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Functions of Golgi ApparatusProcesses Involved
A. Packaging materials1. Fusion with vesicles from ER
B. Association with ER2. Close proximity to ER
C. Formation of glycoproteins3. Modifications in cisternae
D. Formation of glycolipids4. Secreted outside the cell
questions.solution: Packaging involves fusion with ER vesicles, close association with ER, and the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids occurs in the cisternae.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Functions of Cell Wall ComponentsCell Wall Component
A. Strengthens the cell wall1. Cell wall
B. Holds neighboring cells together2. Middle lamella
C. Protects from mechanical damage3. Cellulose
D. Provides rigidity4. Calcium carbonate
questions.solution: Cellulose strengthens the cell wall, the middle lamella holds cells together, the cell wall protects from damage, and calcium carbonate provides rigidity.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Types of VacuolesFunctions
A. Contractile vacuole1. Stores excess water
B. Food vacuole2. Digests engulfed food particles
C. Storage vacuole3. Stores nutrients, waste, and maintains turgor pressure
D. Central vacuole4. Stores substances in plant cells
questions.solution: The contractile vacuole stores excess water, the food vacuole digests engulfed food particles, the storage vacuole stores nutrients and waste, and the central vacuole maintains turgor pressure in plant cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Mitochondrial ComponentsFunctions
A. Outer membrane1. Contains the mitochondrial DNA and ribosomes
B. Inner membrane2. Forms the continuous boundary of the mitochondrion
C. Matrix3. Increases the surface area for reactions
D. Cristae4. Divides the mitochondrion into two compartments
questions.solution: The outer membrane forms the continuous boundary, the inner membrane divides the mitochondrion into compartments, the matrix contains DNA and ribosomes, and the cristae increase the surface area.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Plastid TypesPigments and Functions
A. Chloroplasts1. Store carbohydrates
B. Chromoplasts2. Store oils and fats
C. Leucoplasts3. Store proteins
D. Amyloplasts4. Contain chlorophyll and carotenoids
questions.solution: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoids, chromoplasts store oils and fats, leucoplasts store carbohydrates, and amyloplasts store proteins.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Chloroplast StructuresFunctions
A. Thylakoids1. Site of light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis
B. Grana2. Connects thylakoids between grana
C. Stroma3. Contains enzymes for carbohydrate and protein synthesis
D. Stroma lamellae4. Stacks of thylakoids
questions.solution: Thylakoids are involved in light-dependent reactions, grana are stacks of thylakoids, stroma contains enzymes for synthesis, and stroma lamellae connect thylakoids.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Mitochondrial FunctionsCharacteristics
A. ATP Production1. Increases the surface area for reactions
B. DNA Presence2. Contains the genetic material
C. Ribosomes3. Site of cellular energy production
D. Cristae4. Involved in protein synthesis
questions.solution: ATP production is the main function of mitochondria, DNA is present in the matrix, ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis, and cristae increase the surface area for reactions.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Ribosomal FeaturesDescription
A. 70S Ribosomes1. Found in eukaryotic cells
B. 80S Ribosomes2. Composed of 50S and 30S subunits
C. Outer Membrane3. Composed of 60S and 40S subunits
D. Inner Membrane4. Divides mitochondrial lumen into two compartments
questions.solution: 70S ribosomes have 50S and 30S subunits.80S ribosomes have 60S and 40S subunits.The outer membrane of mitochondria forms the boundary.The inner membrane divides the mitochondrial lumen into two compartments.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cytoskeleton ComponentsFunctions
A. Microtubules1. Movement of fluid or cells
B. Microfilaments2. Mechanical support and cell shape
C. Intermediate Filaments3. Movement of cell or cell contents
D. Cilia4. Support for cell structure and stability
questions.solution: Microtubules provide mechanical support and cell shape.Microfilaments are involved in cell movement.Intermediate filaments offer structural support.Cilia are responsible for movement of fluids or cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Flagellum StructuresComponents
A. Axoneme1. Nine pairs of microtubules arranged in a circle
B. Peripheral Doublets2. Connects central tubules to peripheral doublets
C. Central Tubules3. Runs parallel to the long axis of the flagellum
D. Radial Spokes4. Unconnected by bridges
questions.solution: The axoneme is the core structure of the flagellum with microtubules running parallel.Peripheral doublets are the nine pairs of microtubules arranged in a circle.Central tubules are connected by radial spokes.Radial spokes connect central tubules to peripheral doublets.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Centrosome FeaturesCharacteristics
A. Centrioles1. Cylindrical structures in centrosome
B. Pericentriolar Materials2. Proteinaceous central part in centrioles
C. Triplets of Tubulin3. Surrounding amorphous material
D. Hub4. Each peripheral fibril is a triplet
questions.solution: Centrioles are cylindrical structures in the centrosome.Pericentriolar materials surround the centrioles.Triplets of tubulin form the structure of peripheral fibrils.The hub is the proteinaceous central part of centrioles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Centriole StructuresComponents
A. Peripheral Fibrils1. Central part of centriole
B. Radial Spokes2. Connects peripheral triplets
C. Hub3. Nine evenly spaced fibrils
D. Triplets4. Each peripheral fibril is a triplet
questions.solution: Peripheral fibrils are triplets.Radial spokes connect the peripheral triplets.The hub is the central part of the centriole.Triplets refer to the arrangement of fibrils.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Nuclear ComponentsCharacteristics
A. Chromatin1. Stained by basic dyes and composed of nucleoprotein fibers
B. Nuclear Envelope2. Barrier between nucleus and cytoplasm with a perinuclear space
C. Nucleolus3. Allows movement of RNA and proteins between nucleus and cytoplasm
D. Nuclear Pores4. Site for ribosomal RNA synthesis and not membrane-bound
questions.solution: Chromatin is the nucleoprotein fiber stained by basic dyes.The nuclear envelope forms a barrier with the perinuclear space.The nucleolus is involved in ribosomal RNA synthesis and is not membrane-bound.Nuclear pores are passages for RNA and protein movement.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Chromosome TypesCentromere Position
A. Metacentric1. Centromere near the end, forming one very short and one long arm
B. Sub-metacentric2. Centromere in the middle, forming two equal arms
C. Acrocentric3. Centromere slightly away from the middle, forming one short and one long arm
D. Telocentric4. Centromere at the end, forming one very short arm
questions.solution: Metacentric chromosomes have centromeres in the middle.Sub-metacentric chromosomes have centromeres slightly away from the middle.Acrocentric chromosomes have centromeres near the end.Telocentric chromosomes have centromeres at the end.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Chromosome FeaturesDescriptions
A. Centromere1. Disc-shaped structures on the sides of the centromere
B. Kinetochores2. Holds the two chromatids of a chromosome
C. Chromatids3. Appears as a small fragment due to non-staining constrictions
D. Satellite4. Identical halves of a chromosome
questions.solution: The centromere holds the two chromatids.Kinetochores are disc-shaped structures on the centromere.Satellites appear as small fragments due to non-staining constrictions.Chromatids are the identical halves of a chromosome.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
DNA PackagingDetails
A. Nucleosome1. DNA wrapped around histone proteins
B. Chromatin Fiber2. Visible during cell division
C. Chromosome3. Approximately two meters long in a human cell
D. DNA Thread Length4. Highly extended form of chromatin
questions.solution: Nucleosomes are DNA wrapped around histones.Chromatin fibers are the extended form.Chromosomes are visible during cell division.DNA thread length in a human cell is about two meters.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Chromatin ComponentsTypes of Proteins
A. Histones1. Basic proteins aiding in DNA packaging
B. Non-Histone Proteins2. Part of chromatin and involved in various functions
C. RNA3. Genetic material distributed among chromosomes
D. DNA4. Nucleic acid involved in various functions within chromatin
questions.solution: Histones are basic proteins aiding in DNA packaging.Non-histone proteins are involved in various functions within chromatin.DNA is the genetic material distributed among chromosomes.RNA is a nucleic acid involved in various functions within chromatin.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following is not correct?
options: Schleiden and Schwann formulated the cell theory.
Virchow explained that cells are formed from pre-existing cells
A Unicellular organism carries out its life activities within a single cell.
questions.solution: Robert Brown discovered the cell.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: New cells generate from ___
questions.solution: New cells generate from pre-existing cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following is correct?
options: Cells of all living organisms have a nucleus
Both animal and plant cells have a well defined cell wall
In prokaryotes, there are no membrane bound organelles
Cells are formed de novo from abiotic materials
questions.solution: In prokaryotes, there are no membrane bound organelles
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Mesosomes are present in ____ cells.
questions.solution: Mesosomes are present in Prokaryotic cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following organelles are double membrane bound?
questions.solution: Mitochondria and Chloroplasts are double membrane bound organelles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: ___ organisms have division of labour.
questions.solution: Multicellular organisms have division of labour.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: ____ is the basic unit of life.
questions.solution: Cell is the basic unit of life
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: __ & __ are endomembrane structures.
questions.solution: Lysosomes and Vacuoles are endomembrane structures.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: The nucleus is constrained by the nuclear pore, which is a double membrane called ___.
questions.solution: The nucleus is constrained by the nuclear pore, which is a double membrane called nuclear envelope.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: A common characteristic feature of plant sieve tube cells and most of mammalian erythrocytes is
questions.solution: A common characteristic feature of plant sieve tube cells and most of mammalian erythrocytes is absence of nucleus.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Select one which is not true for ribosomes.
options: Have no role in protein synthesis
questions.solution: Ribosomes are made of two subunits, form polysome and may attach to mRNA. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which one of these is not a eukaryote? .
questions.solution: Anabaena is a cyanobacterium (prokaryote).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following dyes is not used for staining chromosomes?
questions.solution: Safranin stain is not used for staining chromosomes while Basic Fuchsin, Methylene green and Carmine are used for staining chromosomes.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Different cells have different sizes. Arrange the following cells in an ascending order of their size. Choose the correct option among the following:  (i) Mycoplasma  (ii) Ostrich eggs  (iii) Human RBCs  (iv) Bacteria
questions.solution: Ascending order of size:  Mycoplasma < Bacteria < Human RBCs < Ostrich eggs.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following features is common to prokaryotes and many eukaryotes?
questions.solution: Cell wall is present in all prokaryotes (except mycoplasma. and many eukaryotes (like plants and fungi).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Who proposed the fluid mosaic model of plasma membrane?
questions.solution: An improved model of the structure of cell membrane was proposed by  S.J. Singer and G.L. Nicolson (1972) widely accepted as fluid mosaic model.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true for a secretory cell?
options: Rough Endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is easily observed in the cell.
Only Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is present.
Secretory granules are formed in nucleus.
questions.solution: RER is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. RER is well developed in cells engaged in synthesis of secretory products.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: What is a tonoplast?
options: Membrane boundary of the vacuole of plant cells
Cell membrane of a plant cell.
questions.solution: The vacuole is the membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm. The vacuole is bound by a single membrane called tonoplast.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following is not true for an eukaryotic cell?
options: Cell wall is made up of peptidoglycans
It has 80S type of ribosome present in the cytoplasm
questions.solution: In bacteria (prokaryotes) cell wall is made up of peptidoglycan.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following statements is not true for plasma membranes?
options: It is present in both plant and animal cells.
Lipid is present as a bilayer in it. .
Proteins are present integrated as well as loosely associated with the lipid bilayer.
Carbohydrates are never found in it.
questions.solution: Chemical studies showed that the cell membrane is composed of lipids that are arranged in a bilayer. Later, biochemical investigation clearly revealed that the cell membranes also possess protein and carbohydrate.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Plastids differ from mitochondria on the basis of following features? Mark the right answer.
options: Presence of two layers of membrane
questions.solution: Thylakoids are present in plastids but not in mitochondria. Both plastids and mitochondria are similar in presence of two layers of membrane, presence of ribosome and presence of DNA.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Which of the following is not a function of cytoskeleton in a cell?
options: Maintenance of cell shape and structure
questions.solution: The cytoskeleton in a cell are involved in many functions such as mechanical support, motility, and maintenance of the shape of the cell.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: The stain used to visualise mitochondria is
questions.solution: Janus green stain is used to visualise mitochondria.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: What does ‘S’ refer to in a 70S and an 80S ribosome?
questions.solution: Svedberg’s Unit or sedimentation coefficient refers to S in a 70S and an 80S ribosome.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Mention a single membrane bound organelle which is rich in hydrolytic enzymes.
questions.solution: Lysosome is a single membrane bound organelle which is rich in hydrolytic enzymes.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Select the correct statement with respect to polysome?
options: The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosome or polysome.
They do not translate mRNA to protiens
questions.solution: Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosome or polysome. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q: Select the correct statement with respect to satellite.
questions.solution: Sometimes a few chromosomes have non-staining secondary constrictions at a constant location. This gives the appearance of a small fragment called the satellite or trabant.
